subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally block managed Gateway install/refresh when an explicit no-auth configuration would bind outside loopback, even though that changes existing install-time behavior?
rationale: The code matches the existing runtime security boundary, but the earlier failure point can affect existing managed installs and therefore needs maintainer ownership of the compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Accept earlier install block
options.body: Merge the preflight so invalid no-auth non-loopback managed installs fail before service rewrite with actionable remediation.

options.title: Require fuller managed-service proof
options.body: Pause merge until a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service run proves the branch in the actual service refresh path.

options.title: Wait for broader update proof
options.body: Keep this PR paused if maintainers want to solve only the unproven update mutation path rather than the confirmed install boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept earlier install block
recommendation.body: Merge the preflight so invalid no-auth non-loopback managed installs fail before service rewrite with actionable remediation.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows the strongest ownership signal across Gateway runtime startup, no-auth exposure guardrails, and daemon install/auth refactors.
